t: Opposition to apartheid joined African, Indian, coloured and white South Africans in campaigns of defiance, strikes and boycotts and, after the massacre at Sharpeville in 1960, in armed struggle.
Abroad, a worldwide movement of consumer, sports and cultural boycotts, disinvestment and sanctions made South Africa an outcast and added economic pressure to resistance at home.
Township uprisings, sanctions, a costly stalemate and the end of the Cold War brought the government to negotiate from 1990, leading to the first democratic election in April 1994.
dyk: Protest against the South African rugby team’s tour of New Zealand in 1981 was so fierce that during the final Test, at Eden Park in Auckland, a light aircraft flew low over the ground dropping flour bombs onto the pitch.
ev: The National Party wins power and begins to build apartheid into law
The ANC and the South African Indian Congress launch the Defiance Campaign against Unjust Laws
The Congress of the People adopts the Freedom Charter at Kliptown
Police kill 69 protesters at Sharpeville, and the ANC and the PAC are banned
Nelson Mandela and seven others are sentenced to life imprisonment in the Rivonia Trial
The Soweto uprising begins with a schoolchildren’s march against teaching in Afrikaans
F. W. de Klerk unbans the liberation movements, and Mandela is freed after 27 years
South Africa holds its first election open to all, and Mandela becomes president

f.where: South Africa, from the townships of Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban and Port Elizabeth to the rural reserves; the exiled movements in Tanzania, Zambia and Angola; and boycott campaigns in Britain, Europe, North America and the Commonwealth
f.period: 1948–1994: from the National Party’s election victory and the first apartheid laws to the first election open to all South Africans in April 1994
f.figures: Albert Luthuli, Nelson Mandela, Oliver Tambo, Robert Sobukwe, Steve Biko, Desmond Tutu
f.outcome: The negotiated end of apartheid: its laws repealed in 1990–1991, an interim constitution agreed in 1993 and Nelson Mandela elected president in 1994
